contexts.goal: Follow these steps to perform this Touchscreen Responsiveness Issues Troubleshooting.
contexts.title: Touchscreen lag delay

actions.description: It will reduce interference on your device

steps: If your screen protector is peeling or has debris under it, remove it.

actions.description: It will improve responsiveness on your device

steps: If you wish to keep your screen protector on, try enabling the "Touch sensitivity" option.
Go to Settings.
Tap Display.
Tap the switch next to Touch sensitivity.

actionableDeeplink.description: Enables touch sensitivity via device Settings on the device.

steps: If you suspect this is the case, try using a different, undamaged charger.

actions.description: It will switch to navigation buttons

steps: To prevent this, disable the full screen gesture function.
Go to Settings.
Tap Display.
Tap Navigation bar.
Select Buttons to turn off full screen gestures.

actionableDeeplink.description: Opens the navigation bar settings page in device Settings on the device.

steps: To turn off this feature, navigate to Settings, tap Display, and then tap the switch next to Touch sensitivity to disable it.

actionableDeeplink.description: Disables touch sensitivity via device Settings on the device.

steps: If the issue persists after trying all these steps, reach out to Samsung Support for further assistance.
For devices with a Power button: Press and hold the Power button, then tap Restart.
Tap Restart again to confirm.

actions.description: It will restart device using quick settings

steps: For devices with a Side button: Swipe down from the top of the screen with two fingers to open the Quick settings panel.
Tap the Power icon.
Tap Restart.
Tap Restart again to confirm.
If the touchscreen is completely unresponsive, force a restart by pressing and holding the Volume down button and the Power button (or Side button) simultaneously for about 10 seconds.
Once the device turns off, press the Power button or Side button again to turn it back on.

actions.description: It will check third-party app conflicts

steps: Press and hold the Power button (or Side button) and the Volume down button at the same time.
Alternatively, swipe down from the top of the screen with two fingers and tap the Power icon.
Touch and hold Power off.
Tap Safe mode.
Once in Safe mode, try removing any third-party apps that were recently updated or installed around the time the issue began.
Check for updates for any third-party apps you use, as these can sometimes affect gesture customization.
Before proceeding, back up your personal data to avoid losing it.
Navigate to and open Settings.
Tap General management.
Tap Reset.
Tap Factory data reset.
Swipe to and tap Reset.
Tap Delete all.
Enter your Samsung account credentials to complete the reset.
